text:
maria: heads-up: saw a weird sawtooth pattern on prefix cache hit rate starting ~09:14 UTC after the eviction_threshold tweak. backend gRPC CPU spiked and a couple of models started timing out. 
liam: link to alert?

sre-bot: ALERT: kv-cache-backend-high-cpu (sev2) -> https://grafana/redwood/alert/kv-cache-backend-high-cpu

maria: timeline: 09:12 we rolled eviction_threshold from 0.7 -> 0.5 (PR #4872). 09:14 hit-rate dropped from ~0.84 -> 0.22 for a 3m window, then recovered to ~0.7, then dropped again every ~90s (sawtooth). Backend pods hit 95% CPU.
anya: ouch. sawtooth suggests cyclic eviction/rewarm loop. maybe prefetch warmup + eviction fighting?

samir: grabbed KV stats: ```
# curl -s http://internal/kvcache/stats | jq .
{"hit_rate":0.18,"miss_rate":0.82,"active_keys":12034,"evictions_per_min":4300,"avg_kv_latency_ms":28}
```

maria: logs show repeated prefix warmup requests re-fetching same prefixes immediately after eviction: ``[kv] evicted key X, prefetch triggered for key X, fetch->store, evicted again``

kai: also saw batch queue length oscillating. when many misses come in, batching expands window, which increases memory/kv pressure, triggers more evictions -> more misses. feedback loop.

liam: I'm reverting the eviction_threshold change now (rolling back PR #4872). @deploy-bot kickoff?
deploy-bot: deploy started for rollback commit c1a2b3 -> service: kv-cache-config (canary)

maria: doing a quick profile of kernel selection pressure on affected workers. interestingly the kernel chooser moved some short-seq requests to the large-fused kernel under memory pressure which inflated memory working set. attaching snippet: ``kernel_selector: chosen=fused_gemm_large seq=64 mem_est=1.8GB``

samir: that explains worker OOM-ish eviction churn. fused kernel uses bigger activation buffers per batch => more mem => aggressive eviction. we should pin small-seq paths to small kernels when memory utilization > 70%.

anya: temporary mitigation: disable speculative prefetch and lower prefetch concurrency to 16. also reduce batch max-window from 120ms -> 60ms for canaries.

liam: done: config change applied to canary pool: `speculative_prefetch=false, prefetch_concurrency=16, batch_max_window_ms=60`
maria: immediate effect: backend CPU down from 95% -> 58% in ~40s, hit-rate recovered to ~0.66, still some oscillation but amplitude smaller. :thumbsup:

kai: logging from router: ``prefetch_queue_len: 3 -> 0 -> 5 -> 1`` which matches smaller amplitude.

samir: long term: we need bounded kernel selection that considers transient memory pressure + batch window signals. propose: kernel_selector should consult `mem_pressure` metric and pick lower-mem kernel or enforce batch-size caps for fused kernels.

liam: +1. i'll open an RFC. quick TODOs: rollback config change fully, schedule a canary run with new prefetch defaults, add a short-circuit in kernel_selector when `mem_pressure > 0.7`, and add a guard in prefetcher to back off if evictions_per_min > 500.
maria: logging the incident as "eviction-threshold sawtooth -> backend overload" in incidents. I'll take the postmortem.

anya: FYI observed another regression: the KV proxy's cache-key hashing changed in the same deploy (tiny bug in key-normalizer) that made some tenant-specific prefixes inconsistent which reduced effective hit reuse across requests. PR #4869 touched normalizer. might be contributing.

liam: good catch. can we diff the key-normalizer on canary vs prod?
samir: diff shows added `normalize_user_id()` branch that added UID salt for some legacy clients. That likely increased key entropy.

maria: action item bundle: (1) revert eviction_threshold (in progress), (2) revert key-normalizer change or gate it, (3) add prefetch backoff on eviction spikes, (4) kernel_selector mem-pressure guard, (5) postmortem + follow-up RFCs.

kai: also add a perf test: synthetic workload with 90% repeating prefixes + 10% unique to verify rewarm behaviour under eviction. test should run on canary infra and check hit-rate oscillation.

liam: I've queued the revert rollout to full prod after canary stabilizes. deploy-bot: canary healthy -> promoted to prod
deploy-bot: rollout complete -> kv-cache-config reverted

sre-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: emergency config revert performed at 09:28 UTC. Sev2 -> mitigated.

maria: thanks all. follow-up meeting 10:30 UTC to go over postmortem draft. I'll add owners for each TODO in the doc.

anya: quick nits: capture the kernel logs, batch queue histograms, and one-minute eviction-per-min timeseries in the PM. those were key signals.

samir: i've uploaded the flame/heap profile from the worker nodes to the incident folder: s3://redwood-incidents/1765432109/kernel-profiles.tar.gz

maria: final note: avoid simultaneous tuning of eviction + key normalization in future - they interact nonlinearly. :eyes:
